policy_key.x-source: FP-001 typed policy decision contract. The key SYNTAX is a DECLARED INFERENCE; FP-001 states none.

decided_at.x-source: FP-005 requires every change to carry a time. Applying it to the decision itself is a DECLARED INFERENCE.

decision_source.x-source: FP-001 requires the decision to include its reason AND its source.

reason_key.x-source: FP-001 requires a reason; CTR-ERR-001 uses a stable Thai message key, so the reason is a key, not prose.

evaluated_scopes.x-source: FP-002 fixes the precedence platform -> plan -> workspace -> business -> capability. Evaluation always starts at platform and stops somewhere along that order, so the value must be an in-order PREFIX of it. The previous form enforced membership only, and a reversed list and a platform kill switch claiming platform was never evaluated both validated. Independent review showed the order half is expressible here and that declaring it untestable was covering a testable property.

bucket.x-source: FP-003 stable allocation: a workspace stays in the same bucket.

write_disabled.x-source: FP-002 and FP-004: closing writes must still permit historical read.

historical_read_allowed.x-source: FP-002 'historical read still works when write is closed'.

audit.x-source: FP-005 every change carries actor, reason and time; a temporary flag carries an expiry and an owner.

temporary.x-source: FP-005 distinguishes a temporary flag, which must expire and have an owner.

then.x-rule: FP-003: a percentage decision must show the allocation it came from.
FP-002/FP-004: a kill switch is a platform-scope deny that no narrower scope may override.
FP-002: disabling write must not remove historical read.
FP-005: a temporary flag must carry an expiry and an owner.

allOf.x-rule: FP-001: a decision carries its reason AND source, so `default_deny` cannot report effect other than `deny`. Independent review and independent testing both showed default_deny with effect allow validating while only kill_switch was linked.

FP-001: a decision carries its reason AND source, so `explicit_deny` cannot report effect other than `deny`. Independent review and independent testing both showed default_deny with effect allow validating while only kill_switch was linked.

FP-001: a decision carries its reason AND source, so `explicit_allow` cannot report effect other than `allow`. Independent review and independent testing both showed default_deny with effect allow validating while only kill_switch was linked.
